assertions.text: The pay table includes intermediate expected columns (e.g. Regular pay?, Overtime pay?, Premium pay?) so the reader can trace which rule contributes what — not just a single total Weekly pay? column.
assertions.evidence: All three main tables only include a final 'Weekly pay?' column with no intermediate columns. For example, Table 3 shows: 'Scenario | Weekday hrs | Sunday hrs | Holiday hrs | Rate | Weekly pay?' with only the total, not intermediate breakdowns like 'Regular pay?' or 'Overtime pay?'.

assertions.text: The error/rejection table has an expected column (e.g. 'Throws?' or 'Exception?') specifying the exception type per row — rather than hardcoding the exception type in @Description or the method name.
assertions.evidence: @TableTest table for negativeHourlyRateRejected includes a 'Throws?' column with 'IllegalArgumentException' specified per row: 'Negative rate | {0, 40} | 0 | 0 | -10.00 | IllegalArgumentException'

assertions.text: Overtime threshold boundary is covered: at least a value at the threshold (40) and just above (41 or similar). Not just values well below and well above.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 includes rows 'Under threshold | 39', 'At threshold | 40', 'One hour over | 41', providing boundary values at and just above the 40-hour threshold.

assertions.text: A combined scenario is present: a row with weekday + Sunday + holiday hours, testing the composition of all hour types.
assertions.evidence: Table 3 includes row 'All hour types | 50 | 8 | 8 | 20.00 | 1740.00' with all three hour types combined: 50 weekday, 8 Sunday, 8 holiday.

assertions.text: Error/edge cases covered: at least negative hours (floored at zero) and negative or missing rate (rejected).
assertions.evidence: The code tests negative rate (Table 4: 'Negative rate | {0, 40} | 0 | 0 | -10.00 | IllegalArgumentException'), but there is no test row with negative hours to demonstrate the floor rule. The design notes state 'with non-negative inputs, pay can't naturally go below zero' but no actual negative hours row is present in any table.

assertions.text: Sunday and Holiday hour columns use empty cells (not 0) when those inputs are not relevant to a scenario — making it easier to spot which rows involve weekend/holiday hours. This is a readability preference; parameter types should be Integer (not int) to support null from blank cells.
assertions.evidence: The code uses `int` primitives (e.g., 'int weekdayHrs, int sundayHrs') rather than `Integer` wrapper class, so null values cannot be supported. Additionally, Tables 1 and 2 omit irrelevant columns entirely (Table 1 has no Sunday/Holiday columns; Table 2 has no Weekday column) rather than showing empty cells in those columns.

assertions.text: Scenario names describe work patterns (e.g. 'Part-time', 'Five hours overtime', 'Full Sunday shift') — not 'Test case 1' or expected outcomes.
assertions.evidence: All scenario names describe patterns: 'Zero hours', 'Under threshold', 'One hour over', 'Sunday hours only', 'All hour types', 'Zero rate, floor holds', 'Negative rate'. None use generic labels like 'Test case 1' or restate expected outcomes.

assertions.text: Expected values in intermediate and total columns are arithmetically correct for every row, consistent with the formulas in @Description.
assertions.evidence: The model verifies arithmetic: '41 hrs: 40×10 + 1×15 = 415 ✓', '45 weekday + 8 Sunday: regular 40×20=800, overtime 5×20×1.5=150, Sunday 8×20×2=320, total=1270 ✓', '50+8+8: 40×20=800, 10×20×1.5=300, 8×20×2+8×20×2=640, total=1740 ✓'. All match formulas in @Description ('hours × rate', 'hours above 40 × rate × 1.5', 'hours × rate × 2').

assertions.text: Value sets are only used where all values in the set produce the same expected result (e.g. any rate × 0 = 0). Not used where results would differ.
assertions.evidence: The value set `{0, 40}` in the negativeHourlyRateRejected table is used on weekday hrs, with both values expected to throw IllegalArgumentException for rate -10.00. The design notes confirm: 'asserts the rate check fires regardless of how many hours were worked' — both values produce the same exception result.

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: All four test methods have @DisplayName: 'Weekday overtime threshold', 'Sunday and holiday double time', 'Full weekly pay with mixed hour types', 'Negative hourly rate rejected'.

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the pay calculation method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as the overtime threshold (40 hours), premium multipliers (Sunday 2×, Holiday 2.5×), or other fixed assumptions not visible in the table. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show.
assertions.evidence: All main pay calculation methods (Tables 1–3) have @Description. Table 1 provides 'Regular weekday pay: hours × rate (up to 40 hours). Overtime pay: hours above 40 × rate × 1.5.' Table 3 explains 'Sunday and holiday: hours × rate × 2. Total cannot go below 0.' These express formulas and thresholds not visible in table columns alone.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: All four test methods follow the order @DisplayName → @Description → @TableTest, e.g.: '@DisplayName("Weekday overtime threshold") @Description(...) @TableTest(...) void weekdayOvertimeThreshold(...)'.

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All multi-line @Description annotations use triple-quoted strings: '@Description("""...Sunday and holiday hours are 0 for all rows...""")', with no use of string concatenation with '+'.

assertions.text: A row where the hourly rate is zero, showing that pay is zero regardless of hours worked. This is a distinct edge case from negative rate (which is rejected).
assertions.evidence: Table 3 includes row 'Zero rate, floor holds | 40 | 8 | 8 | 0.00 | 0.00', which sets rate to 0.00 with 40 weekday hours and 8 Sunday/holiday hours each, expecting pay of 0.00. This is distinct from the negative rate row in Table 4, which throws an exception.

assertions.text: The test method body contains no if/ternary null-handling or parsing logic. Null-to-default conversion (e.g. blank Sunday hours → 0) is handled via a @TypeConverter method or a private helper, keeping the test method limited to arrange/act/assert.
assertions.evidence: All test method bodies contain only arrange/act/assert logic. Example: 'void weekdayOvertimeThreshold(...) { assertEquals(0, expectedPay.compareTo(calculator.calculate(weekdayHrs, 0, 0, rate))); }' — no if/ternary statements or parsing logic.
